Class AmwpInitEater

java.lang.Object
java.io.InputStream
org.aetheris.wire.AmwpInitEater
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
public final class AmwpInitEater extends InputStream
The AmwpInitEater class wraps a raw terminal input stream. The first read may discard one leading AMWP Init frame. AMWP is the framed protocol on the connection. That frame would otherwise be echoed as chat> N followed by U+FFFD, because the CRC byte is 0x4E. The guard runs only on the first read. Later octets pass through unchanged. The class does not write an acknowledgement. // @aa-sdd G-18 aetheris-stages-1-3.finalize.md

  • Method Details

    • read

      public int read() throws IOException
      The method reads one byte from the source. The first call disarms the guard. End of stream on that first byte is returned as is. A first byte that is not AMWP magic is returned as is. A first byte that is magic is parsed as a frame. An Init frame is discarded, and the method returns the next source byte. A magic frame that is not a successful Init is also consumed, and the method returns the next source byte. Later calls return the next source byte unchanged.
      Specified by:
      read in class InputStream
      Returns:
      The return value is the next byte, or -1 at end of stream.
      Throws:
      IOException - The method throws this when the source read fails.

      public int read(byte[] buf, int off, int len) throws IOException
      The method reads into a buffer, starting with read(). A null buffer returns 0. A length of 0 or less returns 0. End of stream on the first byte returns -1. Further bytes are copied only while the source reports bytes already available.

    • consumeInit

      private boolean consumeInit(int first) throws IOException
      The method reads the rest of a header that began with a magic byte and parses the frame. End of stream before the header is complete returns false. A parse failure returns false. A parsed frame whose type is Init returns true. Any other parsed type returns false. The header and payload bytes are consumed either way.
      Parameters:
      first - The first value is the magic byte already read.
      Returns:
      The return value is true when an Init frame was discarded.
      Throws:
      IOException - The method declares this because the source read declares it.
